title: Rigveda 10.180: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.180: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.180 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 151v-152r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.180.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 38); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 151v
translation.original_text:
1pra sa̍sāhiṣe puruhūta̱ śatrū̱ñ jyeṣṭha̍s te̱ śuṣma̍ i̱ha rā̱tir a̍stu | indrā bha̍ra̱ dakṣi̍ṇenā̱ vasū̍ni̱ pati̱ḥ sindhū̍nām asi re̱vatī̍nām ||
2mṛ̱go na bhī̱maḥ ku̍ca̱ro gi̍ri̱ṣṭhāḥ pa̍rā̱vata̱ ā ja̍ganthā̱ para̍syāḥ | sṛ̱kaṁ sa̱ṁśāya̍ pa̱vim i̍ndra ti̱gmaṁ vi śatrū̍n tāḻhi̱ vi mṛdho̍ nudasva ||
translation.text:
1O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty. In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches.
2Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance. Whetting thy bolt and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 151v (OPenn image 151, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.179.2 ‹vimadhyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 152r, begins in RV 10.180.3 ‹vāmam ojo 'jāyathā vṛṣabha›. Verses 10.180.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.180.3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 38); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 152r
translation.original_text: <sup>3</sup>indra̍ kṣa̱tram a̱bhi vā̱mam ojo 'jā̍yathā vṛṣabha carṣaṇī̱nām | apā̍nudo̱ jana̍m amitra̱yanta̍m u̱ruṁ de̱vebhyo̍ akṛṇor u lo̱kam ||
translation.text: <sup>3</sup>Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o'er the people. Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 152r (OPenn image 151, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.180.3 ‹vāmam ojo 'jāyathā vṛṣabha›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 152v, begins in RV 10.182.1 ‹nayatu durgahā tiraḥ punar›. Verse 10.180.3 ends on this page; 10.180.3 begins on fol. 151v.
